title: Parenthesis
description: Parenthesis String (PS) consists of two parenthesis symbols ‘(’ and ‘)’ only. In parenthesis strings, some strings are called a valid PS (shortly, VPS). Let us give the formal definition of VPS. A single “( )” is a member of VPS, called the base VPS. Let x and y be a member of VPS. Then “(x)”, a VPS which encloses a VPS x with a single pair of parenthesis, is also a member of VPS. And xy, the concatenation of two VPS x and y, is a member of VPS. For example, “(())()” and ((()))” are all VPS, but “(()(”, “(())()))” and “(()” are not VPS. You are given a set of PS. You should decide if the input string is VPS or not.
inputDesc: Your program is to read from standard input. The input consists of T test cases. The number of test cases T is given in the first line of the input. Then PS’s are given in the following T lines one by one. The length of each PS is between 2 and 50, inclusively.
outputDesc: Your program is to write to standard output. Print the result in each line. If the input string is a VPS, then print “YES”. Otherwise print “NO”.
